label: text
text: The China Light and Power Company's station was partially affected yesterday by some of their workmen leaving. There was a further walk out this morning. Arrangements, however, are in hand for replacing the coolies and firemen, and it is not anticipated that the lighting service will be affected in any way.

label: text
text: On inquiry from the company's management the "China Mail" was informed that preparations had already been made and that the supply of current would be maintained.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Electric Company's installation at North Point also lost their workmen this morning.

label: text
text: The men who left were the greasers, oilers, coal coolies and unskilled hands.

label: text
text: The strike of workers on craft in the harbour received a further extension this morning when all the men on the Cheung Chau ferry boats stopped work on orders received from the Seamen's Union in Canton. The ferry service was at a standstill this morning, but arrangements had been made in advance for such a contingency, and the ser-the men on the Cheung Chau mediately. The inconvenience caused to residents on the island will be therefore only temporary.

label: text
text: The decision of the employees on the ferry boats has apparently influenced the servants at European residences at Cheung Chau. During the past two days the workers started to leave the houses, but on finding out that they were liable to be arrested as idlers, they started to come back. According to a telephone message received at police headquarters this morning, all the servants have left.

label: text
text: Other craft affected are the small ferries running to Tai O, Aberdeen, Shaukiwan and Kowloon City. These all stopped running this morning. No arrangements have so far been made for the resumption of these services.

label: text
text: MANNING THE GOOD SHIP TUNG ON

label: text
text: Without a Chinese passenger on board, the 8.s. Tung On arrived at Hongkong from Canton yesterday afternoon, leaving been worked by European and Japanese passengers. Such was the determination and co-operation of the Volunteers that the boat beat her own record and arrived three hours ahead of time.

label: text
text: The duties were then apportioned out, Chief Engineer C. Pike taking charge of the stockhold. Second Engineer Mr. J. Lewis (assisted by the Third Engineer) that of the engine room. Capt. Muir and Chief Officer Fulan relieved each other at the wheel with Mr. A. Jenner, of Kowloon, lending a hand when clearing the shallows. Everyone else took spells of duty and lots were drawn for times. It so fell that one European and one Japanese were allocated a boiler each for spells of an hour.

label: text
text: The Chinese crew had deserted within a few hours of the boat's arrival in Canton from Hongkong and the Chinese passengers who boarded were given the option of giving a hand with the work or getting out. They chose the latter course.

label: text
text: Those who took part in the exploit were Messrs. M. A. Annett, H. T. Buxton, A. E. Quin, T. Dawson, Y. de Barros, A. Hoffmeister (Danish: Consul), J. Struthers, C. F. Crowles, J. H. Mitchell, C. Pokuda, Y. Bojiki, J. Orihashi, T. Kituda, and Dr. Miki all of the Shamden.

label: text
text: In order that communication with Shameen may be maintained regularly and that there may be additional means of food transport to the naval tugs which have been running from Hongkong the s.s. Tung On, brought down last night by European and Japanese passengers, left this morning manned by a crew from the naval boats in the harbour.

label: text
text: The Government have issued tickets (which are at an increased rate) and in spite of the fact that the number of Chinese leaving was not so large as usual a goodly sum was collected.

label: text
text: Revenue officers are acting as ticket collectors and they left with the boat this morning. It is understood that a regular service will be maintained.

label: text
text: The selling of meat at the Central Market was extended into the afternoon yesterday by some of the stalls doing business under police protection. There was a plentiful supply sufficient for all needs, and the extended hours to a certain extent prevent a rush on the stalls.

label: text
text: The total amount of bank-notes in circulation on June 30, 1925, was $54,823,072.

label: text
text: Four men armed with a revolver and daggers gained admittance to the first floor of No. 164 Queen's Road East, shortly before noon yesterday. After binding and gagging the inmates the robbers escaped with a haul of over $3,500 in money, jewellery and clothing.

label: text
text: It is learned that with the permission of the Secretary of Chinese Affairs, a Hongkong Labour Maintenance Association has been formed with its temporary headquarters at the Wuh Keu (Overseas Chinese) Hotel, Connaught Road Central. The object of the Association is to help workmen who have gone on strike or who are forced to strike by intimidation to obtain work or to remain at their present posts.

text:
The Police Force is to lose for a few weeks the services of a well-known and efficient member as a result of a collision in which a motor cycle and side car and a P.W.D. lorry were concerned.
Sergt. A. Nichelbest known to his friends as Lofty "owing, needless to say to his fine physique was returning at the time to the Police Headquarters yesterday morning along Lower Albert Road and the nature of the damage to his machine leaves no doubt as to the reason for the collision which is confirmed by eye-witnesses.

label: text
text: The P.W.D. lorry was being driven by an emergency driver, an Indian, who was proceeding in the opposite direction to Sergt. Nicoll and who, as he approached the nasty corner at the junction of the road with Ice House Street, (outside St. Paul's House and just past the Dairy Farm) either through inexperience or to ensure getting round easier took a wide sweep to the right.

label: text
text: The motor cycle and side car were jammed against the wall of St. Paul's house, and the door of the.lorry is thought to have caught Sergt. Nitoll's knee which was considerably lacerated, but not seriously the "China Mail" was informed on enquiry at the Government Civil Hospital. The forks of the cycle were bent and the state of the footboards speaks eloquently of the force of the collision. An Indian sergeant who was in the side car at the time was uninjured.

label: text
text: Sergt. Nicollusras, taken to Hospital at once. He is proceeding as well as can be expected and is likely to be out in three or four weeks' time.

text: M. Pila, the French Minister at Bangkok, commenting in the "Temps" on the Franco-Siamese Treaties, emphasizes the development of economical relations between France and Siam and the purely defensive aims of the Siamese Army.

label: text
text: He concludes the Franco-Siamese rapprochement is diplomatically evidenced by the treaties which French opinion and Parliament have to ratify. Our Colonies need good neighbours and Siam is a neighbour whose friendship is very useful and the easiest to gain.

label: text
text: The Eastern News Agency of Peking states that the Japanese Minister has strongly protested to the Chinese Government in regard to the Hankow, Kukiang, Chinkiang, and Canton riots, reserving the right to demand compensation for the damage to Japanese lives and property when the facts have been fully investigated.

label: text
text: The Yorozu considers that the recent interviews between Sir Charles Eliot, British Ambassador at Tokyo, and Baron Shidehara foreshadow an Anglo-Japanese understanding for co-operation for the maintenance of peace in the Far East, similar to the former alliance. It considers that Prince Chichibu's unexpected reference to the fine spirit animating the former alliance helps to confirm this belief.

text: Count Aisuke Kabayama has been elected to the Upper House, and Count Michimasa Soveshima has been-unseated-owing-to his outspokenness on the Far Eastern situation, against the Soviet.

label: text
text: This morning's papers refer guardedly to the alleged plot against the Throne last month, saying that the Supreme Court will shortly try the offence under Article 73 of the Criminal Law. It is alleged that four Koreans are implicated.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail).

label: text
text: Sir,—Assurances have been given regarding food-supplies for the European communities of the Colony. Little has been said about the provision of food for the loyal ones among the Chinese. To day profiteers are making hay while the sun shines, getting all they can out of the Chinese who are carrying-on, if not rendering public service.

label: text
text: In fairness to the latter I respectfully submit that an assurance be also given that the Chinese will not be wanting for food. Even if food is available steps should be taken to prevent prices being pushed up when the demand has decreased.

label: text
text: Abnormal circumstances require abnormal measures. Why not regulate food prices, control the supply of food for all, or better still let the authorities take over all stocks in the Colony and pay for same as decreed in the Government Gazette.

label: text
text: European residents have been much inconvenienced but their usual suppliers are not profiteers. Those who enter entirely for the Chinese are not conscientious. My contention is that they should be given no opportunity to exploit the Chinese community. But, first of all, it is necessary to know that the show is to be had in the Colony — hence the necessity for an assurance.
